newsitem.title: FRANCE: S&P cuts AGF CPA rating to AA minus.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts AGF CPA rating to AA minus.

text.p: European rating agency S&P ADEF said on Tuesday it had cut its claims paying ability (CPA) rating for French insurer Assurance Generales de France to AA minus from AA.
S&P said in a statement it had left its rating for AGF short-term debt unchanged at A1.
The rating agency said AGF's CPA rating had been cut because of an anticipated slowdown in the profitability of the group due to heightened competition in the insurance market in France.
S&P said, "Moreover, although AGF has a good capitalisation, it is unlikely the group will reach the high levels of equity capital registered in the past."

"Among its strong points, AGF enjoys an excellent position in the corporate insurance market in France, and is a European leader on the export credit insurance market. However, Standard and Poor's thinks the company needs to take strategic decisions in order to maintain and extend its position in an increasingly competitive environment," the statement said.
S&P also said it foresees more stable financial results for the group.

"These elements, together with the better access of the company to capital markets since its privatisation in May 1996, should contribute to increasing the group's financial and strategic flexibility and maintain its ratings at an excellent levels," S&P said.
